solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Unrealistic hopes of seeing rooks flying?

parts.note: in chess a rook is also called a castle
something flying is up aloft, off the ground

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher's fanciful dreams of spotting rooks on the wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rooks' looks like birds, but here they are the chess pieces, also called castles.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names daydreams or plans with no foundation, wishes that will never be realised.

clue.text: Gardener's headwear means forehead ultimately unseen

parts.note: a cap is a piece of headwear
means, as in capacity or resources to do something, can be ability
the brow is the forehead

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word unseen

explanation.surface: A gardener wears a hat, which means the tip of his forehead stays hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'Gardener' is a link ('is'). Capability Brown was the celebrated 18th-century English landscape gardener.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancelot 'Capability' Brown designed the grounds of many English country estates, the most famous landscape designer of his era.

clue.text: Notices rotten branch

indicators.note: rotten suggests something decayed and falling apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone spots that a tree limb has decayed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notices' reads as a verb; its letters are rearranged, signalled by 'rotten'.
explanation.definitionFit: A branch of an organisation is one division or department of it.

clue.text: Article influences rightwinger

parts.note: to lead someone is to influence them
a Tory is a British Conservative, on the political right

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece sways a conservative reader.
explanation.definitionFit: The main article on a newspaper's front page is called its headline piece, the top news item.

clue.text: Balloon's brilliant in America

definitions.meaning: to balloon is to expand or bulge
in American slang, ... means excellent or great

explanation.definitionFit: To swell is to grow larger like a balloon, and Americans say swell for something excellent.

clue.text: Criminal in Totnes changed plea

indicators.note: in places the criminal's word within the rearranged town name
changed tells us the letters of the town name are altered in order

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal

explanation.surface: A crook in a Devon town alters his plea in court.
explanation.walkthrough: Totnes is a small market town in Devon, England; 'changed' rearranges it to NOTEST, and 'in' places the criminal inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea of nolo contendere is one in which the defendant neither admits nor disputes the charge.

clue.text: Woman regularly thrilled by Austria

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the word thrilled, here the even ones

parts.note: A is the international vehicle code for Austria

explanation.surface: A woman is delighted by a trip to Austria.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilda is a female given name, so it can stand for a woman.

clue.text: Rolls Royce punctured — some support from spouse needed

indicators.note: punctured means pierced, so the word for some is broken open by the car

parts.note: some means any, as in 'have you got any'
a Rolls Royce is an example of a luxury car, a limo

explanation.surface: A luxury car has a flat tyre, and the wife needs a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punctured' suggests a flat tyre, but it signals insertion; 'needed' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Maintenance payments made to a former partner after divorce are this kind of financial support.

clue.text: Fairy tale character remains on the Spanish circus apparatus with family

parts.note: a rump is the remnant left of something, as in the Rump Parliament
el is Spanish for the
stilts are used by circus performers to walk tall
kin means family or relatives

explanation.surface: A storybook figure stands on circus stilts along with his relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grimms' tale features an imp who spins straw into gold and whose name must be guessed.

clue.text: Whole canine statue carried by attendant

indicators.note: carried by means held inside, so the dog letter and the statue sit within the attendant

parts.note: a page is a young attendant or servant
C is an abbreviation for canine, as in a canine tooth
a ka is an ancient Egyptian statue housing the spirit of the dead

explanation.surface: A servant hauls about a complete dog statue.
explanation.walkthrough: A ka, the Egyptian tomb statue, is a crossword favourite; 'carried by' puts the two short pieces inside the attendant.
explanation.definitionFit: A package is a whole set of things offered together, as in a package deal.

clue.text: Scotsman circles islands finding metal

indicators.note: circles means goes round, so the man's name surrounds the islands

parts.note: Calum is a typical Scottish man's name
CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: A Scot sails round some islands and discovers metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finding' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Calcium is a soft grey metallic element, found in bones and limestone.

clue.text: French wine, having tea out, close to religious ecstasy

indicators.note: out means the tea is taken away from the wine

parts.note: Chablis is a white wine from Burgundy
cha (or char) is British slang for tea

indicators.note: close to means the end letter of the word religious

explanation.surface: A tipsy cleric, swapping tea for French wine, nears a spiritual high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Religious ecstasy' looks like one phrase, but 'religious' only gives its last letter; 'out' removes the tea from the wine, leaving BLIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Bliss is a state of perfect joy, the same rapture as ecstasy.

clue.text: Old tenor composed, taking week off somewhere in Canaries

parts.note: Mario Lanza was an American tenor and film star of the 1950s

indicators.note: off means the week letter is removed

parts.note: composed music means wrote it

explanation.surface: A singer from yesteryear wrote songs while on a week's holiday in the Canary Islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Composed' looks like an anagram signal, but it means WROTE; 'taking week off' removes W to leave ROTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanzarote is one of the Canary Islands, a Spanish group off north-west Africa.

clue.text: Swimmer got us exercising in channel

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged words within the channel

parts.note: a lane is a channel, for instance a swimming lane

indicators.note: exercising suggests working the words over, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A swimmer working out in their lane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' suggests a person, but it is a sea creature; 'exercising' rearranges GOT US to GOUST, and 'in' places it in the channel.
explanation.definitionFit: The langouste is a spiny lobster, a crustacean that swims in the sea.

clue.text: Pesto mixture left in marinade, as it were

indicators.note: left in means placed and kept inside, so the mixed letters go into the soaking word

parts.note: to marinade food is to soak it

indicators.note: mixture tells us the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A cook leaves a pesto blend steeping in a marinade, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixture' rearranges the sauce to TOSPE, and 'left in' places it in the soaking word.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases flag that words are being used loosely or figuratively, in a manner of speaking.

clue.text: Idiot traverses near depths of sea

indicators.note: traverses means goes across, so the fool's word spans the other

parts.note: an ass is a fool or idiot
by means near, as in standing by the door

explanation.surface: A fool wades across close to the ocean floor.
explanation.definitionFit: An abyss is a very deep chasm, especially the ocean depths.

clue.text: Country fellow in harbour first to leave

indicators.note: in puts the man inside the shortened harbour
first to leave means the initial letter departs

parts.note: a marina is a harbour for small boats
a gent is a gentleman, a fellow

explanation.surface: A man in a harbour is the first to set sail for a distant country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First to leave' drops the harbour's opening letter to give ARINA; 'in' then places the fellow inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentina is a nation in South America.

clue.text: Now, daughter's advancing to crawl

indicators.note: advancing means moving further along, so the daughter's letter shifts later in the word

parts.note: today means now, at the present time
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A father notices his little girl has just learnt to crawl.
explanation.walkthrough: D moves one place back in TODAY to give TOADY; 'to' is a link before the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To toady is to grovel or fawn, the same as to crawl to someone.

clue.text: Fan provides such voice alongside footballer initially down

parts.note: an air is a tune or melody, something voiced in song

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of footballer

parts.note: low means down, as in low spirits

explanation.surface: A supporter sings, standing beside a player who has been brought down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fan' looks like a football supporter, but it is a cooling device; 'alongside' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan moves air around a room, producing a current of moving air.

clue.text: Italian singer produces note, very soft one, fronted by African people

indicators.note: fronted by means the African nation goes before the soft letters and one

parts.note: ti is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
Togo is a West African nation, its people
BB is a very soft pencil lead grade
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An Italian vocalist hits a gentle note, introduced by Africans.
explanation.walkthrough: Tito Gobbi was a famous Italian baritone (1913-84). 'Fronted by' puts the African nation ahead of the soft pencil grade and one.
explanation.definitionFit: Tito Gobbi was a celebrated Italian operatic baritone, famed for Scarpia in Tosca.

clue.text: Under order to keep tidy hospital

parts.note: be neat is an order to keep things tidy

explanation.surface: Junior staff are told to keep the ward tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Beneath and under are synonyms, both meaning lower than or below.

clue.text: Reject the Netherlands map during drill

indicators.note: during means within, so the country and map go inside the drill

parts.note: a borer is a tool for drilling holes
NL is the international code for the Netherlands
OS is the Ordnance Survey, the British national mapping agency

explanation.surface: A soldier is turned down after mishandling a Dutch map on manoeuvres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Map' is OS, the Ordnance Survey, Britain's official mapping agency; 'during' puts the country and map inside the drill.
explanation.definitionFit: A reject is someone always failing, a person destined never to succeed.

clue.text: Allison is missing, touring South American plain

indicators.note: missing means the second word is removed from the name's letters
touring suggests travelling around, so the remaining letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman goes missing on a trip across the South American grasslands.
explanation.walkthrough: ALLISON without IS leaves ALLON, rearranged by 'touring'.
explanation.definitionFit: A llano is a broad grassy plain, especially in Venezuela and Colombia.

clue.text: Disciple backing an emperor

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the article and ruler are read in reverse

parts.note: a tsar was an emperor of Russia

explanation.surface: A follower supports an emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like support, but it reverses A TSAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rastafarian is a follower of the faith that reveres Haile Selassie, so a devotee.

clue.text: Retrospective part of joint musical piece

indicators.note: retrospective means looking back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a tenon is the projecting part of a mortise and tenon joint

explanation.surface: A backward look at part of a joint musical work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of' looks like a hidden word signal, but it is the definition of TENON, which is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a composition for nine instruments or voices.

clue.text: Excused from work, operating educational chiefs have half

parts.note: a machine that is on is operating
LEA is a Local Education Authority, the old British council body running schools

indicators.note: half takes the second half of the word have

explanation.surface: Head teachers given time off are only half-present.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone granted official absence from duty, a soldier or employee, is said to be away on leave.

clue.text: Brush and pump — equipment needed in Cortina?

parts.note: to skim is to brush lightly over a surface
to pump someone is to question them, to ask

explanation.surface: A list of a cleaner's tools.
explanation.walkthrough: Cortina is Cortina d'Ampezzo, an Italian ski resort, not the Ford car once common on British roads.
explanation.definitionFit: A balaclava-style face covering protects skiers from cold at resorts such as Cortina.

clue.text: Anthony and Mark wore pants for race around boroughs

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, signalling the letters are a mess and rearranged

explanation.surface: Two men wore trousers to run a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like trousers, but it is the anagram signal; 'and' joins the fodder. The race passes through all five boroughs.
explanation.definitionFit: The marathon course runs through Staten Island, Brooklyn, Queens, the Bronx and Manhattan, the city's boroughs.
